title: AFTER IT PASSED
author: Ensemble
question: What does the world record of the catastrophes that almost happened, and who decides that a near miss counts?
medium: An animated dial centred on Earth with sound: every asteroid passage inside the Moon's distance appears, and sounds, on the day the record learned of it, not the day it passed; a date scrubber, a switch between what the record knew then and what it says now, a figure of arcs from passage to first observation, and a table of the thirteen objects that came down and have no row.
embodies: THE RECORD ARRIVES LATE, AND THE HIT IS NOT IN IT. Of 1627 passages closer than the Moon, 765 were first observed after they had gone; a counter shows, for any past date, how many had already passed while the record knew nothing. The thirteen that did not miss are in the catalogue and absent from the close-approach table for their last day: a near miss counts only if it missed.
form: A dial, a clock with sound, a scrubber, an arc figure, a table.
form_argument: The missing datum is temporal: the record writes a passage on the day of its first observation. Only a work that runs in time can show the gap between the two, and sound makes the delay audible: a late passage is heard on the day it was learned.
the_rule_the_work_kept: Passages, distances and first observations only from JPL's own APIs; the impact list cited and checked against JPL; the angle of a streak is declared not data; no risk estimated; precovery named as a reason the late count is a lower bound.

siblings.field: Who keeps the close calls (study 7, 2026-10-10): four keepers of nuclear close calls agree on 3 of 53 events. This record has one keeper and one fixed line; its gap is the passages nobody saw.
siblings.atelier: The Hinge (cycle 007, session 1): in nuclear close calls the keeper who writes the hinge sets how near the miss was. Here nearness is a distance, and what is written later is the sighting.
siblings.atelier_handoff_answered: ho-2026-10-09-atelier-2: the counterfactual is written by a reader, never by the database. In this record the database writes it as a three-sigma interval; in 7 rows the interval reaches inside the Earth.

atlas_neighbours.opened: Atlas entry and its source page summary
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There the invisible marks are chosen and stay invisible. Here no one hides a mark; it is missing until a telescope's observation reaches the record, and then appears late, in time.

atlas_neighbours.title: data-verse (trilogy)
atlas_neighbours.daylight: There scientific data is shown entire, as a sublime. Here the record is shown as it grew, with its gap, and its sound comes on the day a passage was learned.
